newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives pledge to cut capital gains tax.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives pledge to cut capital gains tax.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservative Party, declaring that higher taxes deter enterprise, promised on Wednesday to continue to reduce the burden of capital gains tax and inheritance tax "as it is prudent to do so". The party's manifesto for the May 1 election said it would also reduce the small companies rate of corporation tax in line with personal taxation as progress is made towards acheiving the goal of a 20 percent standard income tax rate.

It also vowed to reform business rates to reduce the cost that falls upon small businesses. "Capital is ever more mobile, flying around the world to places where the tax on it is low: Britain must be one of those places." it said.

Prime Minister John Major said earlier on BBC Radio that the goal of cutting capital gains and inheritance taxes would not take priority over another plank of the manifesto -- plans to reform personal taxation to help families looking after children or relatives by allowing one partner's unused personal allowance to be transferred to a working spouse. The manifesto said it would provide a targeted tax reduction to those families that needed most. About two million one-taxpayer couples would gain up to nine hundred pounds a year, it said.
